templates.name: Pset_ActionRequest
templates.definition: An action request is a request for an action to fulfill a need.  HISTORY: IFC4: Removed RequestSourceType, RequestDescription, Status

entries.name: RequestSourceLabel
entries.definition: A specific name or label that further qualifies the identity of a request source. In the event of an email, this may be the email address.

entries.name: RequestSourceName
entries.definition: The person making the request, where known.

entries.name: RequestComments
entries.definition: Comments that may be made on the request.

templates.name: Pset_ActorCommon
templates.definition: A property set that enables further classification of actors, including the ability to give a number of actors to be designated as a population, the number being specified as a property to be dealt with as a single value rather than having to aggregate a number of instances of IfcActor.

entries.name: NumberOfActors
entries.definition: The number of actors that are to be dealt with together in the population.

entries.name: ActorCategory
entries.definition: Designation of the category into which the actors in the population belong.

entries.name: SkillLevel
entries.definition: Skill level exhibited by the actor and which indicates an extent of their capability to perform actions on the artefacts upon which they can act.

templates.name: Pset_ActuatorPHistory
templates.definition: Properties for history of actuators.HISTORY Added in IFC4.

entries.name: PositionHistory
entries.definition: Indicates position of the actuator over time where 0.0 is fully closed and 1.0 is fully open.

entries.name: QualityHistory
entries.definition: Indicates the quality of measurement or failure condition, which may be further qualified by the Status.  True: measured values are considered reliable; False: measured values are considered not reliable (i.e. a fault has been detected); Unknown: reliability of values is uncertain.

entries.name: StatusHistory
entries.definition: Indicates an error code or identifier, whose meaning is specific to the particular automation system.  Example values include: 'ConfigurationError', 'NotConnected', 'DeviceFailure', 'SensorFailure', 'LastKnown, 'CommunicationsFailure', 'OutOfService'.

entries.name: FailPosition
entries.definition: Specifies the required fail-safe position of the actuator.

entries.name: ManualOverride
entries.definition: Identifies whether hand-operated operation is provided as an override (= TRUE) or not (= FALSE). Note that this value should be set to FALSE by default in the case of a Hand Operated Actuator.

entries.name: ActuatorApplication
entries.definition: Indicates application of actuator.

templates.name: Pset_ActuatorTypeElectricActuator
templates.definition: A device that electrically actuates a control element.

entries.name: ActuatorInputPower
entries.definition: Maximum input power requirement.

entries.name: ElectricActuatorType
entries.definition: Enumeration that identifies electric actuator as defined by its operational principle.

entries.name: ControlPulseCurrent
entries.definition: The current of the electric actuator control pulse.

templates.name: Pset_ActuatorTypeHydraulicActuator
templates.definition: A device that hydraulically actuates a control element.

entries.name: InputPressure
entries.definition:
Maximum input or design pressure for the object.

Maximum design pressure for the actuator.

entries.name: InputFlowrate
entries.definition:
Maximum input flowrate requirement.

Hydraulic flowrate.

templates.name: Pset_ActuatorTypeLinearActuation
templates.definition:
Characteristics of linear actuation of an actuator

entries.name: Force
entries.definition: Indicates the maximum close-off force for the actuator.

entries.name: Stroke
entries.definition: Indicates the maximum distance the actuator must traverse.

templates.name: Pset_ActuatorTypePneumaticActuator
templates.definition: A device that pneumatically actuates a control element

entries.name: InputPressure
entries.definition:
Maximum input or design pressure for the object.

Control air pressure.

entries.name: InputFlowrate
entries.definition:
Maximum input flowrate requirement.

Control air flowrate.

templates.name: Pset_ActuatorTypeRotationalActuation
templates.definition:
Characteristics of rotational actuation of an actuator

entries.name: Torque

entries.name: RangeAngle

templates.name: Pset_Address
templates.definition: This Property Set represents an address for delivery of paper based mail and other postal deliveries.

entries.name: Purpose
entries.definition: Indication of the purpose of this object

entries.name: Description
entries.definition: The Description of the object.

entries.name: UserDefinedPurpose
entries.definition: Allows for specification of user specific purpose of the address beyond the enumeration values provided by Purpose attribute of type IfcAddressTypeEnum. When a value is provided for attribute UserDefinedPurpose, in parallel the attribute Purpose shall have enumeration value USERDEFINED.

entries.name: InternalLocation
entries.definition: An organization defined address for internal mail delivery.

entries.name: AddressLines
entries.definition: The postal address.NOTE  A postal address may occupy several lines (or elements) when recorded. It is expected that normal usage will incorporate relevant elements of the following address concepts: A location within a building (e.g. 3rd Floor) Building name (e.g. Interoperability House) Street number (e.g. 6400) Street name (e.g. Alliance Boulevard). Typical content of address lines may vary in different countries.

entries.name: PostalBox
entries.definition: An address that is implied by an identifiable mail drop.

entries.name: Town
entries.definition: The name of a town.

entries.name: Region
entries.definition: The name of a region.EXAMPLE  The counties of the United Kingdom and the states of North America are examples of regions.

entries.name: PostalCode
entries.definition: The code that is used by the country's postal service.

entries.name: Country
entries.definition: The two letter country code (from ISO 3166).

entries.name: TelephoneNumbers
entries.definition: The list of telephone numbers at which telephone messages may be received.

entries.name: FacsimileNumbers
entries.definition: The list of fax numbers at which fax messages may be received.

entries.name: PagerNumber
entries.definition: The pager number at which paging messages may be received.

entries.name: ElectronicMailAddresses
entries.definition: The list of Email addresses at which Email messages may be received.

entries.name: WWWHomePageURL
entries.definition: The world wide web address at which the preliminary page of information for the person or organization can be located.NOTE  Information on the world wide web for a person or organization may be separated into a number of pages and across a number of host sites, all of which may be linked together. It is assumed that all such information may be referenced from a single page that is termed the home page for that person or organization.

entries.name: MessagingIDs
entries.definition: IDs or addresses for any other means of telecommunication, for example instant messaging, voice-over-IP, or file transfer protocols. The communication protocol is indicated by the URI value with scheme designations such as irc:, sip:, or ftp:.

templates.name: Pset_AirSideSystemInformation
templates.definition: Attributes that apply to an air side HVAC system.HISTORY New property set in IFC Release 1.0.

entries.name: Description
entries.definition: The Description of the object.

entries.name: AirSideSystemType
entries.definition: This enumeration specifies the basic types of possible air side systems (e.g., Constant Volume, Variable Volume, etc.).

entries.name: AirSideSystemDistributionType
entries.definition: This enumeration defines the basic types of air side systems (e.g., SingleDuct, DualDuct, Multizone, etc.).

entries.name: EnergyGainTotal
entries.definition: The total amount of energy gains for the spaces served by the system during the peak cooling conditions, plus any system-level total energy gains.

entries.name: EnergyGainSensible
entries.definition: The sum of total energy gains for the spaces served by the system during the peak cooling conditions, plus any system-level sensible energy gains.

entries.name: EnergyLoss
entries.definition: The sum of energy losses for the spaces served by the system during the peak heating conditions.

entries.name: InfiltrationDiversitySummer
entries.definition: Diversity factor for Summer infiltration.

entries.name: InfiltrationDiversityWinter
entries.definition: Diversity factor for Winter infiltration.

entries.name: ApplianceDiversity
entries.definition: Diversity of appliance load.

entries.name: HeatingTemperatureDelta
entries.definition: Heating temperature difference for calculating space air flow rates.

entries.name: CoolingTemperatureDelta
entries.definition: Cooling temperature difference for calculating space air flow rates.

entries.name: Ventilation
entries.definition: Required outside air ventilation.

entries.name: FanPower
entries.definition: Fan motor loads contributing to the cooling load.

templates.name: Pset_AirTerminalBoxPHistory
templates.definition: Air terminal box performance history attributes.

entries.name: DamperPosition
entries.definition: Control damper position, ranging from 0 to 1; damper position (0=closed=90deg position angle, 1=open=0deg position angle).

entries.name: AtmosphericPressure
entries.definition: Ambient atmospheric pressure.

entries.name: Sound
entries.definition: Sound performance.

templates.name: Pset_AirTerminalBoxTypeCommon
templates.definition: Air terminal box type common attributes.

entries.name: Reference
entries.definition: Reference ID for this specified type in this project (e.g. type 'A-1'), Also referred to as "construction type". It should be provided as an alternative to the name of the "object type", if the software does not support object types and no classification reference to a recognized classification system used.IFC4.3.0.0 DEPRECATION  The Reference property is deprecated and shall no longer be used, use attribute Name on the relating type instead.

entries.name: Status
entries.definition: Status of the element, predominately used in renovation or retrofitting projects. The status can be assigned to as "New" - element designed as new addition, "Existing" - element exists and remains, "Demolish" - element existed but is to be demolished,  "Temporary" - element will exists only temporary (like a temporary support structure).

entries.name: AirFlowRateRange
entries.definition: Possible range of airflow that can be delivered.

entries.name: AirPressureRange
entries.definition: Allowable air static pressure range at the entrance of the air terminal box.

entries.name: NominalAirFlowRate
entries.definition: Nominal air flow rate.

entries.name: ArrangementType
entries.definition:
Terminal box arrangement.
SingleDuct: Terminal box receives warm or cold air from a single air supply duct.
DualDuct: Terminal box receives warm and cold air from separate air supply ducts.

entries.name: ReheatType
entries.definition: Terminal box reheat type.

entries.name: HasSoundAttenuator
entries.definition: If TRUE, the object has sound attenuation.

entries.name: HasReturnAir
entries.definition: Terminal box has return air mixed with supply air from duct work.

entries.name: HasFan
entries.definition: Terminal box has a fan inside (fan powered box).

entries.name: NominalInletAirPressure
entries.definition: Nominal airflow inlet static pressure.

entries.name: NominalDamperDiameter
entries.definition: Nominal damper diameter.

entries.name: HousingThickness
entries.definition: Air terminal box housing material thickness.

entries.name: OperationTemperatureRange
entries.definition:
Allowable operation ambient air temperature range.

Allowable operational range of the ambient air temperature.

entries.name: ReturnAirFractionRange
entries.definition: Allowable return air fraction range as a fraction of discharge airflow.

templates.name: Pset_AirTerminalOccurrence
templates.definition: Air terminal occurrence attributes attached to an instance of IfcAirTerminal.

entries.name: AirFlowRate
entries.definition:
Air flow rate.

The actual airflow rate as designed.

entries.name: AirTerminalLocation
entries.definition: Location  (a single type of diffuser can be used for multiple locations); high means close to ceiling.

templates.name: Pset_AirTerminalPHistory
templates.definition: Air terminal performance history common attributes.

entries.name: AirFlowRateHistory
entries.definition: Volumetric flow rate.

entries.name: NeckAirVelocity
entries.definition: Air velocity at the neck.

entries.name: SupplyAirTemperatureHeating
entries.definition: Supply air temperature in heating mode.

entries.name: SupplyAirTemperatureCooling
entries.definition: Supply air temperature in cooling mode.

entries.name: PressureDrop
entries.definition:
Pressure drop.

Drop in total pressure between inlet and outlet at nominal air-flow rate.

entries.name: InductionRatio
entries.definition: Induction ratio versus distance from the diffuser and its discharge direction; induction ratio (or entrainment ratio) is the ratio of the volumetric flow rate in the jet to the volumetric flow rate at the air terminal.

entries.name: CenterlineAirVelocity
entries.definition: Centerline air velocity versus distance from the diffuser and temperature differential; a function of distance from diffuser and temperature difference between supply air and room air.

templates.name: Pset_AirTerminalTypeCommon
templates.definition:
Air terminal type common attributes.
SoundLevel attribute deleted in IFC2x2 Pset Addendum: Use IfcSoundProperties instead.

entries.name: Reference
entries.definition: Reference ID for this specified type in this project (e.g. type 'A-1'), Also referred to as "construction type". It should be provided as an alternative to the name of the "object type", if the software does not support object types and no classification reference to a recognized classification system used.IFC4.3.0.0 DEPRECATION  The Reference property is deprecated and shall no longer be used, use attribute Name on the relating type instead.

entries.name: Status
entries.definition: Status of the element, predominately used in renovation or retrofitting projects. The status can be assigned to as "New" - element designed as new addition, "Existing" - element exists and remains, "Demolish" - element existed but is to be demolished,  "Temporary" - element will exists only temporary (like a temporary support structure).

entries.name: AirTerminalShape
entries.definition: Shape of the air terminal. Slot is typically a long narrow supply device with an aspect ratio generally greater than 10 to 1.

entries.name: FaceType
entries.definition: Identifies how the terminal face of an AirTerminal is constructed.

entries.name: SlotWidth
entries.definition: Slot width.

entries.name: SlotLength
entries.definition: Slot length.

entries.name: NumberOfSlots
entries.definition: Indicates the number of  slots.

entries.name: FlowPattern
entries.definition: Flow pattern.

entries.name: AirFlowRateRange
entries.definition:
Possible range of airflow that can be delivered.

Air flowrate range within which the air terminal is designed to operate.

entries.name: TemperatureRange
entries.definition:
Allowable maximum and minimum temperature.

Temperature range within which the air terminal is designed to operate.

entries.name: DischargeDirection
entries.definition:
Discharge direction of the air terminal.Parallel: discharges parallel to mounting surface designed so that flow attaches to the surface.
Perpendicular:  discharges away from mounting surface.
Adjustable: both parallel and perpendicular discharge.

entries.name: ThrowLength
entries.definition: The horizontal or vertical axial distance an airstream travels after leaving an AirTerminal before the maximum stream velocity is reduced to a specified terminal velocity under isothermal conditions at the upper value of the AirFlowrateRange.

entries.name: AirDiffusionPerformanceIndex
entries.definition: The Air Diffusion Performance Index (ADPI) is used for cooling mode conditions. If several measurements of air velocity and air temperature are made throughout the occupied zone of a space, the ADPI is the percentage of locations where measurements were taken that meet the specifications for effective draft temperature and air velocity.

entries.name: FinishType
entries.definition: The type of finish for the air terminal.

entries.name: FinishColour
entries.definition: The finish colour of the object.

entries.name: AirTerminalMountingType
entries.definition:
The way the air terminal is mounted to the ceiling, wall, etc.Surface: mounted to the surface of something (e.g., wall, duct, etc.).
Flat flush: mounted flat and flush with a surface.
Lay-in: mounted in a lay-in type ceiling (e.g., a dropped ceiling grid).

entries.name: CoreType
entries.definition: Identifies the way the core of the AirTerminal is constructed.

entries.name: CoreSetHorizontal
entries.definition: Degree of horizontal (in the X-axis of the LocalPlacement) blade set from the centerline.

entries.name: CoreSetVertical
entries.definition: Degree of vertical (in the Y-axis of the LocalPlacement) blade set from the centerline.

entries.name: HasIntegralControl
entries.definition: If TRUE, a self powered temperature control is included in the AirTerminal.

entries.name: FlowControlType
entries.definition: Type of flow control element that may be included as a part of the construction of the air terminal.

entries.name: HasSoundAttenuator
entries.definition: If TRUE, the object has sound attenuation.

entries.name: HasThermalInsulation
entries.definition: If TRUE, the air terminal has thermal insulation.

entries.name: NeckArea
entries.definition: Neck area of the air terminal.

entries.name: EffectiveArea
entries.definition: Effective discharge area of the air terminal.

entries.name: AirFlowrateVersusFlowControlElement
entries.definition: Air flowrate versus flow control element position at nominal pressure drop.

templates.name: Pset_AirToAirHeatRecoveryPHistory
templates.definition: Air to Air Heat Recovery performance history common attributes.

entries.name: SensibleEffectiveness
entries.definition: Sensible heat transfer effectiveness, where effectiveness is defined as the ratio of heat transfer to maximum possible heat transfer.

entries.name: TotalEffectiveness
entries.definition: Total heat transfer effectiveness: The ratio of heat transfer to the maximum possible heat transfer.

entries.name: TemperatureEffectiveness
entries.definition: Temperature heat transfer effectiveness: The ratio of primary airflow temperature changes to maximum possible temperature changes.

entries.name: DefrostTemperatureEffectiveness
entries.definition: Temperature heat transfer effectiveness when defrosting is active.

entries.name: HumidityEffectiveness
entries.definition: Humidity heat transfer effectiveness: The ratio of primary airflow absolute humidity changes to maximum possible absolute humidity changes.

entries.name: SensibleHeatTransferRate
entries.definition: Sensible heat transfer rate.

entries.name: LatentHeatTransferRate
entries.definition: Latent heat transfer rate.

entries.name: TotalHeatTransferRate
entries.definition: Total heat transfer rate.

entries.name: SensibleEffectivenessTable
entries.definition: Sensible heat transfer effectiveness curve as a function of the primary and secondary air flow rate.

entries.name: TotalEffectivenessTable
entries.definition: Total heat transfer effectiveness curve as a function of the primary and secondary air flow rate.

entries.name: AirPressureDropCurves
entries.definition: Air pressure drop as function of air flow rate.

templates.name: Pset_AlarmPHistory
templates.definition: Properties for history of alarm values.  HISTORY: Added in IFC4.

entries.name: Enabled
entries.definition: Indicates whether alarm is enabled or disabled over time.

entries.name: ConditionHistory
entries.definition: Indicates alarm condition over time.  The range of possible values and their meanings is defined by Pset_AlarmTypeCommon.Condition.  An empty value indicates no present alarm condition.

entries.name: Severity
entries.definition: Indicates alarm severity over time, where the scale of values is determined by the control system configuration.  A zero value indicates no present alarm.

entries.name: Acknowledge
entries.definition: Indicates acknowledgement status where False indicates acknowlegement is required and outstanding, True indicates condition has been acknowedged, and Unknown indicates no acknowledgement is required.  Upon resetting the condition, then acknowledgement reverts to Unknown.

entries.name: UserHistory
entries.definition: Indicates acknowledging user over time by identification corresponding to IfcPerson.Identification on an IfcActor.

entries.definition: Table mapping alarm condition identifiers to descriptive labels, which may be used for interpreting Pset_AlarmPHistory.Condition.

templates.name: Pset_AlignmentCantSegmentCommon
templates.definition: Properties common to the definition of all instances of alignment segment that have designParameters for cant.

entries.name: CantDeficiency
entries.definition: Difference between applied cant and a higher equilibrium cant.

entries.name: CantEquilibrium
entries.definition: Cant at a particular speed at which the vehicle will have a resultant force perpendicular to the running plane.

entries.name: StartSmoothingLength
entries.definition: Length for the circular transition change of curvature at the start of the cant segment, measured from the start of the cant segment to the end of the circular transition change of curvature.

entries.name: EndSmoothingLength
entries.definition: Length for the circular transition change of curvature at the end of the cant segment, measured from the start of the circular transition change of curvature to the end of the cant segment.

templates.name: Pset_AlignmentVerticalSegmentCommon
templates.definition: Properties common to the definition of all instances of alignment vertical segment.

entries.name: StartElevation
entries.definition: Elevation of the start point relative to the mean sea level.

entries.name: EndElevation
entries.definition: Elevation of the end point relative to the mean sea level.

templates.name: Pset_AnnotationContourLine
templates.definition: Specifies properties of a standard curve that has a single, consistent measure value.

entries.name: ContourValue
entries.definition: Value of the elevation of the contour above or below a reference plane.

templates.name: Pset_AnnotationLineOfSight
templates.definition: Specifies the properties of the line of sight. For example, it can be used to define the line of sight visibility at the junction between two roads (particularly between an access road and a public road); or in the design of a stadium or theatre.

entries.name: SetbackDistance
entries.definition: Setback distance from the point of connection on the major element along the axis of the minor element (e.g. distance from a public road at which the line of sigfht is measured.

entries.name: VisibleAngleLeft
entries.definition: Angle of visibility to the left of the access.

entries.name: VisibleAngleRight
entries.definition: Angle of visibility to the right of the access.

entries.name: RoadVisibleDistanceLeft
entries.definition: Distance visible to the left of the access.

entries.name: RoadVisibleDistanceRight
entries.definition: Distance visible to the right of the access.

templates.definition: Specifies particular properties of survey methods to be assigned to survey point set or resulting surface patches

entries.name: AcquisitionMethod

entries.name: AccuracyQualityObtained
entries.definition: A measure of the accuracy quality of survey points as obtained expressed in percentage terms.

entries.name: AccuracyQualityExpected
entries.definition: A measure of the accuracy quality of survey points as expected expressed in percentage terms.

templates.name: Pset_Asset

entries.name: AssetUse

entries.name: MediaContent

entries.name: AudioMode

entries.name: IsOutdoors

entries.name: VideoResolutionHeight
entries.definition: Indicates the number of vertical pixels (the largest native video resolution height).

entries.name: VideoResolutionMode
entries.definition: Indicates video resolution modes.

entries.name: VideoCaptureInterval
entries.definition: Indicates video frame capture time intervals.

entries.name: PanTiltZoomPreset
entries.definition: Indicates pan/tilt/zoom position presets.

entries.name: PanHorizontal
entries.definition: Indicates horizontal range for panning.

entries.name: PanVertical
entries.definition: Indicates vertical range for panning.

entries.name: TiltHorizontal
entries.definition: Indicates horizontal range for pivoting, where positive values indicate the camera rotating clockwise,

entries.name: TiltVertical
entries.definition: Indicates vertical range for pivoting, where 0.0 is level, +90 degrees is looking up, -90 degrees is looking down.

entries.name: Zoom
entries.definition: Indicates the zoom range.

Total nominal heat output as listed by the Boiler manufacturer.

For steam boilers, it is a function of inlet temperature versus steam pressure. For example, DefiningValues(InletTemp, OutletTemp), DefinedValues(null, HeatOutput). The IfcTable is related to IfcPropertyTableValue using IfcMetric and IfcResourceConstraintRelationship.

templates.name: Pset_CableSegmentTypeCableSegment
templates.definition: Electrical cable with a specific purpose to lead electric current within a circuit or any other electric construction. Includes all types of electric cables, mainly several electrical segments wrapped together, e.g. cable, tube, busbar. Note that the number of conductors within a cable is determined by an aggregation mechanism that aggregates the conductors within the cable. A single-core cable is defined in IEV 461-06-02 as being 'a cable having only one core'; a multiconductor cable is defined in IEV 461-06-03 as b eing 'a cable having more than one conductor, some of which may be uninsulated'; a mulicore cable is defined in IEV 461-06-04 as being 'a cable having more than one core'.

templates.definition: Properties for signal handling for an analog controller taking disparate valued multiple inputs and creating a single valued output.  HISTORY: IFC4 adapted from Pset_ControllerTypeCommon and applicable predefined type made specific to FLOATING; ACCUMULATOR and PULSECONVERTER types added; additional properties added to replace Pset_AnalogInput and Pset_AnalogOutput.

entries.name: ControlType
entries.definition:
The type controller, signal modification effected and applicable ports

CONSTANT: No inputs; SignalOffset is written to the output value.
MODIFIER: Single analog input is read, added to SignalOffset, multiplied by SignalFactor, and written to the output value.
ABSOLUTE: Single analog input is read and absolute value is written to the output value.
INVERSE: Single analog input is read, 1.0 is divided by the input value and written to the output value.
HYSTERISIS: Single analog input is read, delayed according to SignalTime, and written to the output value.
RUNNINGAVERAGE: Single analog input is read, averaged over SignalTime, and written to the output value.
DERIVATIVE: Single analog input is read and the rate of change during the SignalTime is written to the output value.
INTEGRAL: Single analog input is read and the average value during the SignalTime is written to the output value.
BINARY: Single binary input is read and SignalOffset is written to the output value if True.
ACCUMULATOR: Single binary input is read, and for each pulse the SignalOffset is added to the accumulator, and while the accumulator is greater than the SignalFactor, the accumulator is decremented by SignalFactor and the integer result is incremented by one.
PULSECONVERTER: Single integer input is read, and for each increment the SignalMultiplier is added and written to the output value.
SUM: Two analog inputs are read, added, and written to the output value.
SUBTRACT: Two analog inputs are read, subtracted, and written to the output value.
PRODUCT: Two analog inputs are read, multiplied, and written to the output value.
DIVIDE: Two analog inputs are read, divided, and written to the output value.
AVERAGE: Two analog inputs are read and the average is written to the output value.
MAXIMUM: Two analog inputs are read and the maximum is written to the output value.
MINIMUM: Two analog inputs are read and the minimum is written to the output value..
INPUT: Controller element is a dedicated input.
OUTPUT: Controller element is a dedicated output.
VARIABLE: Controller element is an in-memory variable.

The expected range and default value. The LowerLimitValue and UpperLimitValue must fall within the physical Range and may be used to determine extents when charting Pset_ControllerPHistory.Value.

entries.name: SignalTime

templates.name: Pset_ControllerTypeProportional
templates.definition: Properties for signal handling for an proportional controller taking setpoint and feedback inputs and creating a single valued output. HISTORY: In IFC4, SignalFactor1, SignalFactor2 and SignalFactor3 changed to ProportionalConstant, IntegralConstant and DerivativeConstant.  SignalTime1 and SignalTime2 changed to SignalTimeIncrease and SignalTimeDecrease.

entries.name: ControlType
entries.definition:
The type controller, signal modification effected and applicable ports

PROPORTIONAL: Output is proportional to the control error. The gain of a proportional control (Kp) will have the effect of reducing the rise time and reducing , but never eliminating, the steady-state error of the variable controlled.
PROPORTIONALINTEGRAL: Part of the output is proportional to the control error and part is proportional to the time integral of the control error. Adding the gain of an integral control (Ki) will have the effect of eliminating the steady-state error of the variable controlled, but it may make the transient response worse.
PROPORTIONALINTEGRALDERIVATIVE: Part of the output is proportional to the control error, part is proportional to the time integral of the control error and part is proportional to the time derivative of the control error. Adding the gain of a derivative control (Kd) will have the effect of increasing the stability of the system, reducing the overshoot, and improving the transient response of the variable controlled.

entries.name: IntegralConstant

entries.name: DerivativeConstant

LOWERLIMITSWITCH: Single analog input is read and if less than Value.LowerBound then True is written to the output value.
UPPERLIMITSWITCH: Single analog input is read and if more than Value.UpperBound then True is written to the output value.
LOWERBANDSWITCH: Single analog input is read and if less than Value.LowerBound+BandWidth then True is written to the output value.
UPPERBANDSWITCH: Single analog input is read and if more than Value.UpperBound-BandWidth then True is written to the output value.
NOT: Single binary input is read and the opposite value is written to the output value.
AND: Two binary inputs are read and if both are True then True is written to the output value.
OR: Two binary inputs are read and if either is True then True is written to the output value.
XOR: Two binary inputs are read and if one is true then True is written to the output value.
CALENDAR: No inputs; the current time is compared with an IfcWorkCalendar to which the IfcController is assigned and True is written if active.

templates.name: Pset_DistributionSystemTypeElectrical
templates.definition: Properties of electrical circuits.

entries.name: ElectricalSystemType
entries.definition:
For certain purposes of electrical regulations, IEC 60364 defines types of system using type identifiers. Assignment of identifiers depends upon the relationship of the source, and of exposed conductive parts of the installation, to Ground (Earth).   Identifiers that may be assigned through IEC 60364 are:•TN type system, a system having one or more points of the source of energy directly earthed, the exposed conductive parts of the installation being connected to that point by protective conductors,
•TN C type system, a TN type system in which neutral and protective functions are combined in a single conductor throughout the system,
•TN S type system, a TN type system having separate neutral and protective conductors throughout the system,
•TN C S type system, a TN type system in which neutral and protective functions are combined in a single conductor in part of the system,
•TT type system, a system having one point of the source of energy directly earthed, the exposed conductive parts of the installation being connected to earth electrodes electrically independent of the earth electrodes of the source,
•IT type system, a system having no direct connection between live parts and Earth, the exposed conductive parts of the electrical installation being earthed.

entries.name: ElectricalSystemCategory
entries.definition: Designates the voltage range of the circuit, according to IEC.  HIGHVOLTAGE indicates >1000V AC or >1500V DV; LOWVOLTAGE indicates 50-1000V AC or 120-1500V DC; EXTRALOWVOLTAGE indicates <50V AC or <120V DC.

entries.name: Diversity
entries.definition:
The ratio, expressed as a numerical
value or as a percentage, of the
simultaneous maximum demand of
a group of electrical appliances or
consumers within a specified period,
to the sum of their individual maximum
demands within the same
period. The group of electrical appliances is in this case connected to this circuit. Definition from IEC 60050, IEV 691-10-04
NOTE1: It is often not desirable to size each conductor in a distribution system to support the total connected load at that point in the network. Diversity is applied on the basis of the anticipated loadings that are likely to result from all loads not being connected at the same time.
NOTE2: Diversity is applied to final circuits only, not to sub-main circuits supplying other DBs.

entries.name: NumberOfLiveConductors
entries.definition: Number of live conductors within this circuit. Either this property or the ConductorFunction property (if only one) may be asserted.

entries.name: MaximumAllowedVoltageDrop
entries.definition:
The maximum voltage drop across the circuit that must not be exceeded.
There are two  voltage drop limit settings that may be applied; one for sub-main circuits, and one in each Distribution Board or Consumer Unit for final circuits connected to that board. The settings should limit the overall voltage drop to the required level. Default settings of 1.5% for sub-main circuits and 2.5% for final circuits, giving an overall limit of 4% may be applied.
NOTE: This value may also be specified as a constraint within an IFC model if required but is included within the property set at this stage pending implementation of the required capabilities within software applications.

entries.name: NetImpedance
entries.definition: The maximum earth loop impedance upstream of a circuit (typically stated as the variable Zs). This value is for 55o C (130oF) Celsius usage.

entries.name: RatedVoltageRange
entries.definition: Voltage range as declared by the manufacturer expressed by its lower and upper rated voltages [Source : IEC 62368-1:2010, 3.3.10.5].

entries.name: AcousticRating

It is provided according to the national building code. It indicates the sound transmission resistance of this object by an index ratio (instead of providing full sound absorption values).

entries.name: SecurityRating

It is giving according to the national building code.

entries.name: DurabilityRating

entries.name: HygrothermalRating

entries.name: WaterTightnessRating

entries.name: MechanicalLoadRating

entries.name: WindLoadRating

entries.name: Infiltration

entries.name: IsExternal

entries.name: ThermalTransmittance

entries.name: GlazingAreaFraction

entries.name: HandicapAccessible

entries.name: FireExit

Indication whether this object is designed to serve as an exit in the case of fire (TRUE) or not (FALSE).

Here it defines an exit door in accordance to the national building code.

entries.name: HasDrive

entries.name: SelfClosing

entries.name: SmokeStop

templates.name: Pset_DoorLiningProperties
templates.definition: Properties of the door lining.HISTORY New property set in IFC4.3.2.0 to replace the entity IfcDoorLiningProperties

entries.name: LiningDepth
entries.definition:
The depth of the lining.

For a door, it is the depth of the door lining, measured perpendicular to the plane of the door lining. If omitted (and with a given value to lining thickness) it indicates an adjustable depth (i.e. a depth that adjusts to the thickness of the wall into which the occurrence of this door style is inserted).

entries.name: LiningThickness
entries.definition:
Thickness of the lining.

For a door, it is the thickness of the door lining as explained in the figure above. If LiningThickness value is 0. (zero) it denotes a door without a lining (all other lining parameters shall be set to NIL in this case). If the LiningThickness is NIL it denotes that the value is not available.

entries.name: ThresholdDepth
entries.definition: Depth (dimension in plane perpendicular to door leaf) of the door threshold. Only given if the door lining includes a threshold. If omitted (and with a given value to threshold thickness) it indicates an adjustable depth (i.e. a depth that adjusts to the thickness of the wall into which the occurrence of this door style is inserted).

entries.name: ThresholdThickness
entries.definition: Thickness of the door threshold as explained in the figure above. If ThresholdThickness value is 0. (zero) it denotes a door without a threshold (ThresholdDepth shall be set to NIL in this case). If the ThresholdThickness is NIL it denotes that the information about a threshold is not available.

entries.name: TransomThickness
entries.definition:
Thickness of the transom.

For a door, it is the thickness (width in plane parallel to door leaf) of the transom (if provided - that is, if the TransomOffset attribute is set), which divides the door leaf from a glazing (or window) above. If the TransomThickness is set to zero (and the TransomOffset set to a positive length), then the door is divided vertically into a leaf and transom window area without a physical frame.

entries.name: TransomOffset
entries.definition: Offset of the transom (if given) which divides the door leaf from a glazing (or window) above. The offset is given from the bottom of the door opening.

entries.name: LiningOffset
entries.definition:
Offset of the lining.

For a door, it is the offset (dimension in plane perpendicular to door leaf) of the door lining. The offset is given as distance to the x axis of the local placement.

entries.name: ThresholdOffset
entries.definition: Offset (dimension in plane perpendicular to door leaf) of the door threshold. The offset is given as distance to the x axis of the local placement. Only given if the door lining includes a threshold and the parameter is known.

entries.name: CasingThickness
entries.definition:
Thickness of the casing.

For a door, it is the dimension in plane of the door leaf. If given it is applied equally to all four sides of the adjacent wall.

entries.name: CasingDepth
entries.definition:
Depth of the casing.

For a door, it is the dimension in the plane perpendicular to door leaf. If given it is applied equally to all four sides of the adjacent wall.

entries.name: LiningToPanelOffsetX
entries.definition:
Offset between the lining and the panel, measured along the x-axis of the local placement.

For a door, it is the offset between the lining and the window panel.

entries.name: LiningToPanelOffsetY
entries.definition:
Offset between the lining and the panel, measured along the y-axis of the local placement.

For a door, it is the offset between the lining and the door panel.

templates.name: Pset_DoorPanelProperties
templates.definition: Properties of the door panel.HISTORY New property set in IFC4.3.2.0 to replace the entity IfcDoorPanelProperties

entries.name: PanelDepth
entries.definition:
Depth of the panel.

For a door, it is the depth of the door panel, measured perpendicular to the plane of the door leaf.

entries.name: PanelOperation
entries.definition:
The way of operation of a panel.

For a door, it is the way of operation of the panel. The PanelOperation of the door panel shall correspond to the OperationType of the IfcDoorType by which it is referenced.

entries.name: PanelWidth
entries.definition:
Width of the panel.

For a door, it is the width of the panel, given as ratio relative to the total clear opening width of the door. If omitted, it defaults to 1. A value shall be provided for all doors with OperationType's at IfcDoorType defining a door with more then one panel.

entries.name: PanelPosition
entries.definition:
Position of the panel.

For a door, it is the position of the panel within the door. The PanelPosition of the door panel shall correspond to the OperationType of the IfcDoorType by which it is referenced.

entries.definition: Thickness of the third (outer) glass layer.

entries.definition: Name of the gas by which the gap between two glass layers is filled. It is given for information purposes only.

entries.definition: Colour (tint) selection for this glazing. It is given for information purposes only.

entries.definition: Indication whether the glass is tempered (TRUE) or not (FALSE) .

entries.definition: Indication whether the glass is layered with other materials (TRUE) or not (FALSE).

entries.definition: Indication whether the glass is coated with a material (TRUE) or not (FALSE).

entries.definition: Indication whether the glass includes a contained wire mesh to prevent break-in (TRUE) or not (FALSE)

entries.name: VisibleLightReflectance
entries.definition: Fraction of the visible light that is reflected by the glazing at normal incidence. It is a value without unit.

entries.name: VisibleLightTransmittance
entries.definition: Fraction of the visible light that passes the object at normal incidence. It is a value without unit.

entries.name: SolarAbsorption
entries.definition: (Asol) The ratio of incident solar radiation that is absorbed by a glazing system. It is the sum of the absorption distributed to the exterior (a) and to the interior (qi). Note the following equation Asol + Rsol + Tsol = 1

entries.name: SolarReflectance
entries.definition: (Rsol): The ratio of incident solar radiation that is reflected by a glazing system (also named ρe). Note the following equation Asol + Rsol + Tsol = 1

entries.name: SolarTransmittance
entries.definition: The ratio of incident solar radiation that directly passes through a system (also named τe). Note the following equation Asol + Rsol + Tsol = 1

entries.name: SolarHeatGainTransmittance
entries.definition: (SHGC): The ratio of incident solar radiation that contributes to the heat gain of the interior, it is the solar radiation that directly passes (Tsol or τe) plus the part of the absorbed radiation that is distributed to the interior (qi). The SHGC is referred to also as g-value (g = τe + qi).

entries.name: ShadingCoefficient
entries.definition: (SC): The measure of the ability of a glazing to transmit solar heat, relative to that ability for 3 mm (1/8-inch) clear, double-strength, single glass. Shading coefficient is being phased out in favor of the solar heat gain coefficient (SHGC), and is approximately equal to the SHGC multiplied by 1.15. The shading coefficient is expressed as a number without units between 0 and 1.

entries.name: ThermalTransmittanceSummer
entries.definition:
Thermal transmittance coefficient (U-Value) of a material.
Summer thermal transmittance coefficient of the glazing only, often referred to as (U-value).

entries.name: ThermalTransmittanceWinter
entries.definition:
Thermal transmittance coefficient (U-Value) of a material.
Winter thermal transmittance coefficient of the glazing only, often referred to as (U-value).

templates.name: Pset_EnvironmentalImpactIndicators
templates.definition:
Environmental impact indicators are related to a given “functional unit” (ISO 14040 concept). An example of functional unit is a "Double glazing window with PVC frame" and the unit to consider is "one square meter of opening elements filled by this product”.
Indicators values are valid for the whole life cycle or only a specific phase (see LifeCyclePhase property). Values of all the indicators are expressed per year according to the expected service life. The first five properties capture the characteristics of the functional unit. The following properties are related to environmental indicators.
There is a consensus agreement international for the five one. Last ones are not yet fully and formally agreed at the international level.

entries.name: WeldLegLength

entries.name: AirParticleFilterType
entries.definition:
A panel dry type extended surface filter is a dry-type air filter with random fiber mats or blankets in the forms of pockets, V-shaped or radial pleats, and include the following:CoarseFilter: Filter with a efficiency lower than 30% for atmosphere dust-spot.
CoarseMetalScreen: Filter made of metal screen.
CoarseCellFoams: Filter made of cell foams.
CoarseSpunGlass: Filter made of spun glass.
MediumFilter: Filter with an efficiency between 30-98% for atmosphere dust-spot.
MediumElectretFilter: Filter with fine electret synthetic fibers.
MediumNaturalFiberFilter: Filter with natural fibers.
HEPAFilter: High efficiency particulate air filter.
ULPAFilter: Ultra low penetration air filter.
MembraneFilters: Filter made of membrane for certain pore diameters in flat sheet and pleated form.
A renewable media with a moving curtain viscous filter are random-fiber media coated with viscous substance in roll form or curtain where fresh media is fed across the face of the filter and the dirty media is rewound onto a roll at the bottom or to into a reservoir:
RollForm: Viscous filter used in roll form.
AdhesiveReservoir: Viscous filter used in moving curtain form.
A renewable moving curtain dry media filter is a random-fiber dry media of relatively high porosity used in moving-curtain(roll) filters.
An electrical filter uses electrostatic precipitation to remove and collect particulate contaminants.

entries.name: ContributedLuminousFlux
entries.definition: Luminous flux is a photometric measure of radiant flux, i.e. the volume of light emitted from a light source. Luminous flux is measured either for the interior as a whole or for a part of the interior (partial luminous flux for a solid angle). All other photometric parameters are derivatives of luminous flux. Luminous flux is measured in lumens (lm). The luminous flux is given as a nominal value for each lamp.

entries.name: LightEmitterNominalPower
entries.definition: Light emitter nominal power.

entries.name: LampMaintenanceFactor
entries.definition: Non recoverable losses of luminous flux of a lamp due to lamp depreciation; i.e. the decreasing of light output of a luminaire due to aging and dirt.

entries.name: LampBallastType
entries.definition:
The type of ballast used to stabilise gas discharge by limiting the current during operation and to deliver the necessary striking voltage for starting. Ballasts are needed to operate Discharge Lamps such as Fluorescent, Compact Fluorescent, High-pressure Mercury, Metal Halide and High-pressure Sodium Lamps.
Magnetic ballasts are chokes which limit the current passing through a lamp connected in series on the principle of self-induction. The resultant current and power are decisive for the efficient operation of the lamp. A specially designed ballast is required for every type of lamp to comply with lamp rating in terms of Luminous Flux, Color Appearance and service life. The two types of magnetic ballasts for fluorescent lamps are KVG Conventional   (EC-A series) and VVG Low-loss ballasts (EC-B series). Low-loss ballasts have a higher efficiency, which means reduced ballast losses and a lower thermal load. Electronic ballasts are used to run fluorescent lamps at high frequencies (approx. 35 - 40 kHz).

entries.name: LampCompensationType
entries.definition: Identifies the form of compensation used for power factor correction and radio suppression.

entries.name: ColourAppearance
entries.definition: In both the DIN and CIE standards, artificial light sources are classified in terms of their colour appearance. To the human eye they all appear to be white; the difference can only be detected by direct comparison. Visual performance is not directly affected by differences in colour appearance.

entries.name: Spectrum
entries.definition: The spectrum of radiation describes its composition with regard to wavelength. Light, for example, as the portion of electromagnetic radiation that is visible to the human eye, is radiation with wavelengths in the range of approx. 380 to 780 nm (1 nm = 10 m). The corresponding range of colours varies from violet to indigo, blue, green, yellow, orange, and red. These colours form a continuous spectrum, in which the various spectral sectors merge into each other.

entries.name: ColourTemperature
entries.definition: The colour temperature of any source of radiation is defined as the temperature (in Kelvin) of a black-body or Planckian radiator whose radiation has the same chromaticity as the source of radiation. Often the values are only approximate colour temperatures as the black-body radiator cannot emit radiation of every chromaticity value. The colour temperatures of the commonest artificial light sources range from less than 3000K (warm white) to 4000K (intermediate) and over 5000K (daylight).

entries.name: ColourRenderingIndex
entries.definition: The CRI indicates how well a light source renders eight standard colours compared to perfect reference lamp with the same colour temperature. The CRI scale ranges from 1 to 100, with 100 representing perfect rendering properties.

templates.name: Pset_ManufacturerTypeInformation

Defines characteristics of types (ranges) of manufactured products that may be given by the manufacturer. Note that the term 'manufactured' may also be used to refer to products that are supplied and identified by the supplier or that are assembled off site by a third party provider.
HISTORY: This property set replaces the entity IfcManufacturerInformation from previous IFC releases. IFC 2x4: AssemblyPlace property added.

entries.name: GlobalTradeItemNumber
entries.definition: The Global Trade Item Number (GTIN) is an identifier for trade items developed by GS1 (www.gs1.org).

entries.name: ArticleNumber
entries.definition: Article number or reference that is be applied to a configured product according to a standard scheme for article number definition as defined by the manufacturer. It is often used as the purchasing number.

entries.name: ModelReference
entries.definition: The model number or designator of the product model (or product line) as assigned by the manufacturer of the manufactured item.

entries.name: ModelLabel
entries.definition: The descriptive model name of the product model (or product line) as assigned by the manufacturer of the manufactured item.

entries.name: Manufacturer

entries.name: ProductionYear
entries.definition: The year of production of the manufactured item.

entries.name: AssemblyPlace

entries.name: OperationalDocument

entries.name: SafetyDocument
entries.definition: Manufacturer's safety document

entries.name: PerformanceCertificate
entries.definition: Manufacturer's performance certificate

entries.name: Berths

templates.name: Pset_MarinePartChamberCommon

entries.name: EffectiveChamberSize

entries.name: StructuralType

templates.name: Pset_MarineVehicleCommon

entries.name: LengthBetweenPerpendiculars

entries.name: VesselDepth

entries.name: VesselDraft

entries.name: AboveDeckProjectedWindEnd

entries.name: AboveDeckProjectedWindSide

entries.name: Displacement

entries.name: CargoDeadWeight

entries.name: LaneMeters

templates.name: Pset_MarineVehicleDesignCriteria

entries.name: AllowableHullPressure

entries.name: SoftnessCoefficient

entries.name: ApproachSpeed

entries.name: MarkerType

entries.name: NominalHeight

entries.name: NominalWidth
entries.definition: The nominal overall width of the object. The size information is provided in addition to the shape representation and the geometric parameters used within. In cases of inconsistency between the geometric parameters and the size properties, provided in the attached property set, the geometric parameters take precedence.

templates.name: Pset_MarkingLinesCommon

entries.name: DashedLine
entries.definition: State if the line is dashed or continuous

entries.name: DashedLinePattern

entries.name: NominalWidth

templates.name: Pset_MaterialCombustion
templates.definition: A set of extended material properties of products of combustion generated by elements typically used within the context of building services and flow distribution systems.

entries.name: SpecificHeatCapacity
entries.definition:
Defines the specific heat capacity of a material.

Specific heat of the products of combustion: heat energy absorbed per temperature unit.

entries.name: N20Content
entries.definition: Nitrous oxide (N2O) content of the products of combustion. This is measured in weight of N2O per unit weight and is therefore unitless.

entries.name: COContent
entries.definition: Carbon monoxide (CO) content of the products of combustion. This is measured in weight of CO per unit weight and is therefore unitless.

entries.name: CO2Content
entries.definition: Carbon dioxide (CO2) content of the products of combustion. This is measured in weight of CO2 per unit weight and is therefore unitless.

templates.name: Pset_MaterialCommon
templates.definition: A set of general material properties.

entries.name: MolecularWeight
entries.definition: Molecular weight of material (typically gas).

entries.name: Porosity
entries.definition: The void fraction of the total volume occupied by material (Vbr - Vnet)/Vbr.

entries.name: MassDensity
entries.definition: Material mass density.

templates.name: Pset_MaterialConcrete
templates.definition: A set of extended mechanical properties related to concrete materials.

entries.name: CompressiveStrength
entries.definition: The compressive strength of the object or material.

entries.name: MaxAggregateSize
entries.definition: The maximum aggregate size of the concrete.

entries.name: AdmixturesDescription
entries.definition: Description of the admixtures added to the concrete mix.

entries.name: Workability
entries.definition: Description of the workability of the fresh concrete defined according to local standards.

entries.name: WaterImpermeability
entries.definition: Description of the water impermeability denoting the water repelling properties.

entries.name: ProtectivePoreRatio
entries.definition: The protective pore ratio indicating the frost-resistance of the concrete.

templates.name: Pset_MaterialEnergy
templates.definition: A set of extended material properties for energy calculation purposes.

entries.name: ViscosityTemperatureDerivative
entries.definition: Viscosity temperature derivative.

entries.name: MoistureCapacityThermalGradient
entries.definition: Thermal gradient coefficient for moisture capacity. Based on water vapor density.

entries.name: ThermalConductivityTemperatureDerivative
entries.definition: Thermal conductivity temperature derivative.

entries.name: SpecificHeatTemperatureDerivative
entries.definition: Specific heat temperature derivative.

entries.name: VisibleRefractionIndex
entries.definition: Index of refraction (visible) defines the "bending" of the sola! r ray in the visible spectrum when it passes from one medium into another.

entries.name: SolarRefractionIndex
entries.definition: Index of refraction (solar) defines the "bending" of the solar ray when it passes from one medium into another.

entries.name: GasPressure
entries.definition: Fill pressure (e.g. for between-pane gas fills): the pressure exerted by a mass of gas confined in a constant volume.

templates.name: Pset_MaterialFuel
templates.definition: A set of extended material properties of fuel energy typically used within the context of building services and flow distribution systems.

entries.name: CombustionTemperature
entries.definition:
Combustion temperature.

Combustion temperature of the material when air is at 298 K and 100 kPa.

entries.name: CarbonContent
entries.definition: The carbon content in the fuel. This is measured in weight of carbon per unit weight of fuel and is therefore unitless.

entries.name: LowerHeatingValue
entries.definition: Lower Heating Value is defined as the amount of energy released (MJ/kg) when a fuel is burned completely, and H2O is in vapor form in the combustion products.

entries.name: HigherHeatingValue
entries.definition: Higher Heating Value is defined as the amount of energy released (MJ/kg) when a fuel is burned completely, and H2O is in liquid form in the combustion products.

templates.name: Pset_MaterialHygroscopic
templates.definition: A set of hygroscopic properties of materials.

entries.name: UpperVaporResistanceFactor
entries.definition: The vapor permeability relationship of air/material (typically value > 1), measured in high relative humidity (typically in 95/50 % RH).

entries.name: LowerVaporResistanceFactor
entries.definition: The vapor permeability relationship of air/material (typically value > 1), measured in low relative humidity (typically in 0/50 % RH).

entries.name: IsothermalMoistureCapacity
entries.definition: Based on water vapor density.

entries.name: VaporPermeability
entries.definition: The rate of water vapor transmission per unit area per unit of vapor pressure differential under test conditions.

entries.name: MoistureDiffusivity
entries.definition: Moisture diffusivity is a transport property that is frequently used in the hygrothermal analysis of building envelope components.

templates.name: Pset_MaterialMechanical
templates.definition: A set of mechanical material properties normally used for structural analysis purpose. It contains all properties which are independent of the actual material type.

entries.name: DynamicViscosity
entries.definition: A measure of the viscous resistance of the material.

entries.name: YoungModulus
entries.definition: A measure of the Young's modulus of elasticity of the material.

entries.name: ShearModulus
entries.definition: A measure of the shear modulus of elasticity of the material.

entries.name: PoissonRatio
entries.definition: A measure of the lateral deformations in the elastic range.

entries.name: ThermalExpansionCoefficient
entries.definition: Quantity characterizing the variation with thermodynamic temperature T of the distance l between two points of a body, under given conditions (IEC 113-04-27). The ratio is defined per Kelvin.

templates.name: Pset_MaterialOptical
templates.definition: A set of optical properties of materials.

entries.name: VisibleTransmittance
entries.definition: Transmittance at normal incidence (visible). Defines the fraction of the visible spectrum of solar radiation that passes through per unit area, perpendicular to the surface.

entries.name: SolarTransmittance
entries.definition: The ratio of incident solar radiation that directly passes through a system (also named τe). Note the following equation Asol + Rsol + Tsol = 1

entries.name: ThermalIrTransmittance
entries.definition: Thermal IR transmittance at normal incidence. Defines the fraction of thermal energy that passes through per unit area, perpendicular to the surface.

entries.name: ThermalIrEmissivityBack
entries.definition: Thermal IR emissivity: back side. Defines the fraction of thermal energy emitted per unit area to "blackbody" at the same temperature, through the "back" side of the material.

entries.name: ThermalIrEmissivityFront
entries.definition: Thermal IR emissivity: front side. Defines the fraction of thermal energy emitted per unit area to "blackbody" at the same temperature, through the "front" side of the material.

entries.name: VisibleReflectanceBack
entries.definition: Reflectance at normal incidence (visible): back side. Defines the fraction of the solar ray in the visible spectrum that is reflected and not transmitted when the ray passes from one medium into another, at the "back" side of the other material, perpendicular to the surface. Dependent on material and surface characteristics.

entries.name: VisibleReflectanceFront
entries.definition: Reflectance at normal incidence (visible): front side. Defines the fraction of the solar ray in the visible spectrum that is reflected and not transmitted when the ray passes from one medium into another, at the "front" side of the other material, perpendicular to the surface. Dependent on material and surface characteristics.

entries.name: SolarReflectanceBack
entries.definition: Reflectance at normal incidence (solar): back side. Defines the fraction of the solar ray that is reflected and not transmitted when the ray passes from one medium into another, at the "back" side of the other material, perpendicular to the surface. Dependent on material and surface characteristics.

entries.name: SolarReflectanceFront
entries.definition: Reflectance at normal incidence (solar): front side. Defines the fraction of the solar ray that is reflected and not transmitted when the ray passes from one medium into another, at the "front" side of the other material, perpendicular to the surface. Dependent on material and surface characteristics.

templates.name: Pset_MaterialSteel
templates.definition: A set of extended mechanical properties related to steel (or other metallic and isotropic) materials.

entries.name: YieldStress
entries.definition: A measure of the yield stress (or characteristic 0.2 percent proof stress) of the material.

entries.name: UltimateStress
entries.definition: A measure of the ultimate stress of the material.

entries.name: UltimateStrain
entries.definition: A measure of the (engineering) strain at the state of ultimate stress of the material.

entries.name: HardeningModule
entries.definition: A measure of the hardening module of the material (slope of stress versus strain curve after yield range).

entries.name: ProportionalStress
entries.definition: A measure of the proportional stress of the material. It describes the stress before the first plastic deformation occurs and is commonly measured at a deformation of 0.01%.

entries.name: PlasticStrain
entries.definition: A measure of the permanent displacement, as in slip or twinning, which remains after the stress has been removed. Currently applied to a strain of 0.2% proportional stress of the material.

entries.name: Relaxations
entries.definition:
Measures of decrease in stress over long time intervals resulting from plastic flow. Different relaxation values for different initial stress levels for a material may be given. It describes the time dependent relative relaxation value for a given initial stress level at constant strain.
Relating values are the "RelaxationValue". Related values are the "InitialStress"

entries.name: StructuralGrade
entries.definition: Classification label to define mechanical properties according to structural grades defined in published standards; designated by numbers, letters, or a combination of both.

templates.name: Pset_MaterialThermal
templates.definition: A set of thermal material properties.

entries.name: SpecificHeatCapacity
entries.definition:
Defines the specific heat capacity of a material.

Defines the specific heat of the material: heat energy absorbed per temperature unit.

entries.name: BoilingPoint
entries.definition: The boiling point of the material (fluid).

entries.name: FreezingPoint
entries.definition: The freezing point of the material (fluid).

entries.name: ThermalConductivity
entries.definition:
The thermal conductivity of the object.

The rate at which thermal energy is transmitted through the material.

templates.name: Pset_MaterialWater
templates.definition: A set of extended material properties for of water typically used within the context of building services and flow distribution systems.

entries.name: IsPotable
entries.definition: If TRUE, then the water is considered potable.

entries.name: Hardness
entries.definition: Water hardness as positive, multivalent ion concentration in the water (usually concentrations of calcium and magnesium ions in terms of calcium carbonate).

entries.name: AlkalinityConcentration
entries.definition: Maximum alkalinity concentration (maximum sum of concentrations of each of the negative ions substances measured as CaCO3).

entries.name: AcidityConcentration
entries.definition: Maximum CaCO3 equivalent that would neutralize the acid.

entries.name: ImpuritiesContent
entries.definition: Fraction of impurities such as dust to the total amount of water. This is measured in weight of impurities per weight of water and is therefore unitless.

entries.name: DissolvedSolidsContent
entries.definition: Fraction of the dissolved solids to the total amount of water. This is measured in weight of dissolved solids per weight of water and is therefore unitless.

entries.name: PHLevel
entries.definition: Maximum water PH in a range from 0-14.

templates.name: Pset_MaterialWood
templates.definition: This is a collection of properties applicable to wood-based materials that specify kind and grade of material as well as moisture related parameters.

entries.name: Species

entries.name: StrengthGrade
entries.definition: Grade with respect to mechanical strength and stiffness.

entries.name: AppearanceGrade
entries.definition: Grade with respect to visual quality.

entries.name: Layup

entries.name: Layers

entries.name: Plies
entries.definition: Number of plies.

entries.name: MoistureContent
entries.definition: Total weight of moisture relative to oven-dried weight of the wood.

entries.name: DimensionalChangeCoefficient
entries.definition: Weighted dimensional change coefficient, relative to 1% change in moisture content.

entries.name: ThicknessSwelling
entries.definition: Swelling ratio relative to board depth.

entries.definition: Determines whether mechanical material properties are applicable to 'ASD' = allowable stress design (working stress design), 'LSD' = limit state design, or 'LRFD' = load and resistance factor design.

Describes the common properties and nominal dimensions of pavement.Property use clarification
The nominal thickness of the pavement remains constant with the value from NominalThickness, unless the property NominalThicknessEnd is provided. In which case NominalThickness is the value at the beginning of a transition (usually at the object placement location). e.g. a (road) transition segment where the pavement object's linear placement along an alignment denotes the beginning location and NominalThicknessEnd is the value at the end as indicated by the property NominalLength. entries.name: BatterAtEnd

entries.name: ShearDeformationAreaY
entries.definition: Area of the profile for calculating the shear deformation due to a shear force parallel to ys. For example measured in mm². If given, the shear deformation area ys shall be non-negative.

entries.name: MaximumSectionModulusY
entries.definition: Bending resistance about the ys axis at the point with maximum zs ordinate. For example measured in mm³.

entries.name: MinimumSectionModulusY
entries.definition: Bending resistance about the ys axis at the point with minimum zs ordinate. For example measured in mm³.

entries.name: MaximumSectionModulusZ
entries.definition: Bending resistance about the zs axis at the point with maximum ys ordinate. For example measured in mm³.

entries.name: MinimumSectionModulusZ
entries.definition: Bending resistance about the zs axis at the point with minimum ys ordinate. For example measured in mm³.

entries.name: TorsionalSectionModulus
entries.definition: Torsional resistance (about xs). For example measured in mm³.

entries.name: ShearAreaZ
entries.definition: Area of the profile for calculating the shear stress due to shear force parallel to the section analysis axis zs. For example measured in mm². If given, the shear area zs shall be non-negative.

entries.name: ShearAreaY
entries.definition: Area of the profile for calculating the shear stress due to shear force parallel to the section analysis axis ys. For example measured in mm². If given, the shear area ys shall be non-negative.

entries.name: PlasticShapeFactorY
entries.definition: Ratio of plastic versus elastic bending moment capacity about the section analysis axis ys. A dimensionless value.

entries.name: PlasticShapeFactorZ
entries.definition: Ratio of plastic versus elastic bending moment capacity about the section analysis axis zs. A dimensionless value.

templates.name: Pset_ProjectOrderChangeOrder
templates.definition: A change order is an instruction to make a change to a product or work being undertake. Note that the change order status is defined in the same way as a work order status since a change order implies a work requirement.

entries.name: ReasonForChange

entries.name: BudgetSource
entries.definition: The budget source requested.

templates.name: Pset_ProjectOrderMaintenanceWorkOrder
templates.definition: A MaintenanceWorkOrder is a detailed description of maintenance work that is to be performed. Note that the Scheduled Frequency property of the maintenance work order is used when the order is required as an instance of a scheduled work order.

entries.name: ProductDescription
entries.definition: A textual description of the products that require the work.

entries.name: WorkTypeRequested
entries.definition: Work type requested in circumstances where there are categorizations of types of work task. It could be used to identify a remedial task, minor work task, electrical task etc.

entries.name: ContractualType
entries.definition: The contractual type of the work.

entries.name: IfNotAccomplished
entries.definition: Comments if the job is not accomplished.

entries.name: MaintenanceType
entries.definition:
Identifies the predefined types of maintenance that can be done from which the type that generates the maintenance work order may be set where:ConditionBased: generated as a result of the condition of an asset or artefact being less than a determined value.
Corrective: generated as a result of an immediate and urgent need for maintenance action.
PlannedCorrective: generated as a result of immediate corrective action being needed but with sufficient time available for the work order to be included in maintenance planning.
Scheduled: generated as a result of a fixed, periodic maintenance requirement.

entries.name: FaultPriorityType
entries.definition:
Identifies the predefined types of priority that can be assigned from which the type may be set where:High: action is required urgently.
Medium: action can occur within a reasonable period of time.
Low: action can occur when convenient.

entries.name: LocationPriorityType
entries.definition:
Identifies the predefined types of priority that can be assigned from which the type may be set where:High: action is required urgently.
Medium: action can occur within a reasonable period of time.
Low: action can occur when convenient.

entries.name: ScheduledFrequency
entries.definition: The period of time between expected instantiations of a work order that may have been predefined.

entries.name: SpecialInstructions

entries.name: IsFOB
entries.definition: Indication of whether contents of the purchase order are delivered 'Free on Board' (= True) or not (= False). FOB is a shipping term which indicates that the supplier pays the shipping costs (and usually also the insurance costs) from the point of manufacture to a specified destination, at which point the buyer takes responsibility.

entries.name: ShipMethod

templates.name: Pset_PropertyAgreement
templates.definition: A property agreement is an agreement that enables the occupation of a property for a period of time.The objective is to capture the information within an  agreement that is relevant to a facilities manager. Design and construction information associated with the property is not considered. A property agreement may be applied to an instance of IfcSpatialStructureElement including to compositions defined through the IfcSpatialStructureElement.Element.CompositionEnum.Note that the associated actors are captured by the IfcOccupant class.

entries.name: AgreementType
entries.definition: Identifies the predefined types of property agreement from which the type required may be set.

entries.name: TrackingIdentifier

entries.name: AgreementVersion
entries.definition: The version number of the agreement that is identified.

entries.name: AgreementDate

entries.name: PropertyName

entries.name: CommencementDate

entries.name: TerminationDate

entries.name: Duration

Duration.

The period of time for the lease.

entries.name: Options

entries.name: ConditionCommencement
entries.definition: Condition of property provided on commencement of the agreement e.g. cold shell, warm lit shell, broom clean, turn-key.

entries.name: Restrictions
entries.definition: Restrictions that may be placed by a  competent authority.

entries.name: ConditionTermination
entries.definition: Condition of property required on termination of the agreement e.g. cold shell, warm lit shell, broom clean, turn-key.

templates.name: Pset_ProtectiveDeviceBreakerUnitI2TCurve
templates.definition: A coherent set of attributes representing a curve for let-through energy of a protective device. Note - A protective device may be associated with different instances of this pSet providing information related to different  basic characteristics

entries.name: VoltageLevel
entries.definition: The voltage levels for which the data of the instance is valid. More than one value may be selected in the enumeration.

entries.name: NominalCurrent
entries.definition:
The nominal current that is designed to be measured.

A set of nominal currents in [A] for which the data of this instance is valid. At least one value shall be provided. Any value in the set shall not exceed the value of the
UltimateRatedCurrent associated with the same breaker unit.

entries.name: BreakerUnitCurve
entries.definition:
A curve that establishes the let through energy of a breaker unit when a particular prospective current is applied.  Note that the breaker unit curve is defined within a Cartesian coordinate system and this fact must be asserted within the property set:(1) Defining value: ProspectiveCurrent: A list of minimum 2 and maximum 16 numbers providing the currents in [A] for points in the current/I2t log/log coordinate space. The curve is drawn as a straight line between two consecutive points.
(2) Defined value: LetThroughEnergy: A list of minimum 2 and maximum 16 numbers providing the let-through energy, I2t, in [A2s] for points in the current/I2t log/log coordinate space. The curve is drawn as a straight line between two consecutive points.

templates.name: Pset_ProtectiveDeviceBreakerUnitI2TFuseCurve
templates.definition: A coherent set of attributes representing curves for melting- and breaking-energy of a fuse. Note - A fuse may be associated with different instances of this property set providing information related to different  basic characteristics.

entries.name: VoltageLevel
entries.definition: The voltage levels for which the data of the instance is valid. More than one value may be selected in the enumeration.

entries.name: BreakerUnitFuseMeltingCurve
entries.definition:
A curve that establishes the energy required to melt the fuse of a breaker unit when a particular prospective melting current is applied.  Note that the breaker unit fuse melting curve is defined within a Cartesian coordinate system and this fact must be:(1) Defining value: ProspectiveCurrentMelting :A list of minimum 2 and maximum 8 numbers providing the currents in [A] for points in the
current/melting_energy log/log coordinate space. The curve is drawn as a straight line between two consecutive points.
(2) Defined value: MeltingEnergy: A list of minimum 2 and maximum 8 numbers providing the energy whereby the fuse is starting to melt, I2t, in [A2s] for points in the current/melting_energy log/log coordinate space. The curve is drawn as a straight line between two consecutive points.

entries.name: BreakerUnitFuseBreakingingCurve
entries.definition:
A curve that establishes the let through breaking energy of a breaker unit when a particular prospective breaking current is applied.  Note that the breaker unit fuse breaking curve is defined within a Cartesian coordinate system and this fact must be:(1) Defining value: ProspectiveCurrentBreaking: A list of minimum 2 and maximum 8 numbers providing the currents in [A] for points in the
current/breaking energy log/log coordinate space. The curve is drawn as a straight line between two consecutive points.
(2) Defined value: LetThroughBreakingEnergy: A list of minimum 2 and maximum 8 numbers providing the breaking energy whereby the fuse has provided a break, I2t, in [A2s] for points in the current/breakting_energy log/log coordinate space. The curve is drawn as a straight line between two consecutive.

(2) Defined value: A list of minimum 2 and maximum 16 numbers providing the let-through peak currents, Î, in [A] for points in the I/Î log/log coordinate space. The curve is drawn as a straight line between two consecutive points.

entries.name: VoltageLevel

UltimateRatedCurrent associated with the same breaker unit.

entries.name: ICS60947
entries.definition: The service breaking capacity in [A] for an object tested in accordance with the IEC 60947 series.

entries.name: ICN60898

entries.name: ICS60898

templates.name: Pset_ProtectiveDeviceBreakerUnitTypeMotorProtection
templates.definition: A coherent set of attributes representing different capacities of a a motor protection device, defined in accordance with IEC 60947. Note - A protective device may be associated with different instances of this Pset.

entries.name: PerformanceClasses
entries.definition:
A set of designations of performance classes for the breaker unit for which the data of this instance is valid.

A set of designations of performance classes for the breaker unit for which the data of this instance is valid. A breaker unit being a motor protection device may be
constructed for different levels of breaking capacities. A maximum of 7 different
performance classes may be provided. Examples of performance classes that may be specified include B, C, N, S, H, L, V.

entries.name: VoltageLevel
entries.definition: The voltage levels for which the data of the instance is valid. More than one value may be selected in the enumeration.

entries.name: ICU60947
entries.definition: The ultimate breaking capacity in [A] for an object tested in accordance with the IEC 60947 series.

entries.name: ICS60947
entries.definition: The service breaking capacity in [A] for an object tested in accordance with the IEC 60947 series.

entries.name: ICW60947

entries.name: ICM60947
entries.definition: The making capacity in [A] for a circuit breaker or motor protection device tested in accordance with the IEC 60947 series.
